html:
SMTO-CMP-0018 — Not every step in a series of commands finished successfully

GUID: 27912abc-dfef-4f2f-9e58-c11b216affcc
Slug: completion-invalid-sequence-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • SMTO ran a series of commands in order, but its records show a step that failed, didn't run, or doesn't match its saved result. So it can't confirm the whole series worked. Finished steps are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's steps and find the command in the series that failed or didn't run. That step is the reason SMTO can't confirm the whole series.
  2. Check on the computer it ran on whether that step's change happened, for example whether a file or service was updated. A failed command can still change things partway, so check before anything is repeated.
  3. Select Resume, or tell SMTO which steps are done and which remain in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task, then select Continue. SMTO keeps the finished steps and can run only what's left.
  4. Don't select Restart task. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so the whole series could run again.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply confirms every step in the series.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't rerun the whole series yourself; earlier steps have already made changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Sequence evidence expansion found mismatched parent step counts or status, missing or stale child IDs, children whose ownership or recorded receipt does not match, or children without successful exited Shell receipts (reason invalid_sequence_evidence).

What this means

  • Sequence expansion finds mismatched parent counts/status, missing or stale child IDs, wrong order/arguments or children without complete successful exited receipts. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Sequence expansion finds mismatched parent counts/status, missing or stale child IDs, wrong order/arguments or children without complete successful exited receipts.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare parent and each original child invocation/receipt, including actual exit state and retained arguments.

How to fix it

  • Compare the sequence manifest (total, attempted and executed steps, failed_step, next_unexecuted_step and closed dispatch) with each child's receipt and invocation record (sequence_evidence in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py). Verify or complete only the failed or unexecuted steps and cite the original child receipts; do not replay completed children.
  • Use the preserved ordered sequence receipts and verify incomplete steps without replaying completed mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Ordered original evidence establishes every required step without replaying completed children.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
